title: Get started with kplotly.r
text: Date POSIXct x gives line, range slider x axis hover shows every series hovered date. Several y columns ("") stacked coloured series. vars argument kplot TSstudio style calls accepted, slider turns range slider : ts object works :
code: set.seed(1) weather <- data.frame(date = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:364) weather$rain <- rgamma(365, 0.4, 0.1) weather$temp <- 12 + 8 * sin(1:365 / 58 - 1.5) + rnorm(365) kplotly(weather, "date", c("rain", "temp"), title = "Weather in 2024") kplotly(weather, vars = list(x = "date", y = "all"), type = "point",         slider = FALSE) kplotly(AirPassengers, title = "Air passengers", theme = "minimal")

title: Get started with kplotly.r
text: type guessed x (line dates, point numbers, bar categories) set type: kply_types() lists . string column names layer legend, () gives fixed value:
code: kply_types() #> [1] "point" "line"  "step"  "area"  "bar"   "col" kplotly(iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species",         size = "Petal.Width", theme = "bw") obs <- data.frame(t = 1:20, v = (1:20)^1.2 + rnorm(20)) sim <- data.frame(t = 1:20, v = (1:20)^1.2) kplotly(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "point") +   kplotly(sim, "t", "v", color = I("black"), type = "line")

title: Get started with kplotly.r
text: + superposes plots: colours shared legend entry shown ; clicking hides level every layer. Pipe-friendly modifiers change plot afterwards:
code: kplotly(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "point") +   kplotly(sim, "t", "v", color = "Simulated", type = "line") +   kplotly(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "line",           line = list(dash = "dot")) kplotly(weather, "date", "temp") |>   kply_add(type = "point", opacity = 0.4) |>   kply_labs(title = "Temperature", y = "°C") |>   kply_theme("inrae") |>   kply_legend("bottom")

title: Get started with kplotly.r
text: palette takes palette name, colours (named fix colour level) function n.
code: kply_themes() #> [1] "default" "minimal" "bw"      "inrae" kply_palettes() #> [1] "plotly"    "inrae"     "okabe_ito" kplotly(weather, "date", c("rain", "temp"), theme = "inrae")

title: Get started with kplotly.r
text: plotly.js attribute reachable: trace attributes ... kplotly() (line = list(width = 1), opacity, connectgaps…); layout attributes kply_layout(), configuration kply_config(); function htmlwidget added +, applied last (e.g. htmlwidgets::onRender()). as_htmlwidget() returns widget, Shiny (htmlwidgets::shinyRenderWidget()) save ; kply_save() writes HTML file.
code: kplotly(weather, "date", "rain", type = "bar") |>   kply_layout(yaxis = list(type = "log")) |>   kply_config(locale = "fr")

title: Get started with kplotly.r
text: Types, themes palettes live registries: new input class needs as_kdata() method returning data frame.
code: kply_register_type(   "linepoint", list(type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers"),   color = c("marker.color", "line.color"), sort = TRUE ) kply_register_palette("traffic", c("#2ecc71", "#f1c40f", "#e74c3c")) kply_register_theme("traffic", list(plot_bgcolor = "#fafafa"),                     palette = "traffic") kplotly(pressure, "temperature", "pressure", type = "linepoint",         theme = "traffic")

what: Concise, Composable Interactive Plots from a Single Call
title: Concise, Composable Interactive Plots from a Single Call
text: Site: https://kbosirany.github.io/kplotly.r/ (development version: /dev) interactive plot several series, shared legend range slider quickly costs dozen lines plot_ly() / add_trace() / layout() calls long-format bookkeeping. kplotly.r draws complete interactive plot one short call, plots stay composable kplotly S3 class. plotly.js counterpart kggplot, arguments: changing kggplot( kplotly( turns static plot interactive one. plotly.js embedded (“cartesian” bundle): kplotly.r depends htmlwidgets, plotly R package dependencies.

title: Concise, Composable Interactive Plots from a Single Call
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("kbosirany/kplotly.r")

title: Concise, Composable Interactive Plots from a Single Call
text: See vignette("kplotly") (“Get started”) full tour. Branch, version release conventions kpkg.r: vignette("workflow", package = "kpkg.r").
code: library(kplotly.r)  # A time series: several columns, a range slider and a unified hover weather <- data.frame(date = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:364) weather$rain <- rgamma(365, 0.4, 0.1) weather$temp <- 12 + 8 * sin(1:365 / 58 - 1.5) kplotly(weather, "date", c("rain", "temp"), title = "Weather")  # kplot / TSstudio style calls kplotly(weather, vars = list(x = "date", y = "all"), type = "point")  # Superpose layers: shared colours, one legend entry per level obs <- data.frame(t = 1:20, v = (1:20)^1.2 + rnorm(20)) sim <- data.frame(t = 1:20, v = (1:20)^1.2) kplotly(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "point", theme = "inrae") +   kplotly(sim, "t", "v", color = "Simulated", type = "line")  # Any plotly.js layout attribute, and the htmlwidget for Shiny p <- kplotly(iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species") |>   kply_layout(hovermode = "x") as_htmlwidget(p)

code: # scatter plot, coloured, themed: one call kplotly(iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species",         title = "Iris", theme = "inrae")  # a time series: several columns at once, with a range slider d <- data.frame(   date = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:99,   rain = rgamma(100, 0.5, 0.2),   temp = 10 + 5 * sin(1:100 / 15) ) kplotly(d, "date", "all", title = "Weather")  # the same, with the kplot / TSstudio style `vars` kplotly(d, vars = list(x = "date", y = c("rain", "temp")), type = "point")  # superpose a second dataset: consistent colours and a shared legend obs <- data.frame(t = 1:10, v = cumsum(rep(1, 10))) sim <- data.frame(t = 1:10, v = cumsum(rep(1.2, 10))) kplotly(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "point") +   kplotly(sim, "t", "v", color = "Simulated", type = "line")
